title: Review a gala acknowledgment batch: deductible amounts and required wording for eight payments
instructions: Dana Whitcomb has the Lanterns & Letters gala acknowledgments (CRM batch GALA-26-03, eight payments) ready to merge and send. Before anything goes out, review every payment against our receipting policy and the gala fact sheet. For each one, give me the deductible amount, what its acknowledgment must state and must not state, and any correction Dana needs to make in the CRM. I approve this batch, so write it as the review I will sign off from.

criteria.title: Whitfield tickets: deductible amount $420
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-01 (Marcus and Leah Whitfield, two individual tickets, $750) a deductible amount of $420 — the $750 payment less the two seats' good-faith value of $330 (2 × $165). FAIL if it gives any other deductible amount, such as $750 or $0, or values the two seats at anything other than $330 (for example $750, at the $375 ticket price).

criteria.title: Whitfield acknowledgment carries the quid pro quo disclosure
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review says P-01's acknowledgment must describe the two gala seats (dinner, bar and entertainment), give the good-faith estimate of their value as $330, and include the statement that the deductible amount is limited to the excess of the payment over the value of the goods and services provided. FAIL if it says P-01's acknowledgment needs no such disclosure, says no goods or services were provided to the Whitfields, or gives an estimate other than $330.

criteria.title: Lighthouse sponsorship benefits valued at $2,050
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review values the goods and services provided for P-02 (Drs. Elena and Paul Vasquez-Hart, Lighthouse Sponsor, $10,000) at $2,050 — 10 seats × $165 ($1,650) plus the VIP reception for 10 guests × $40 ($400) — and assigns no value to the program and signage listing. FAIL if it values those benefits at any other figure — such as the CRM's $3,750 (ten seats at the $375 ticket price), $1,650 (reception left out) or $4,150 — or puts a dollar value on the name listing.

criteria.title: Lighthouse sponsorship deductible amount $7,950
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-02 a deductible amount of $7,950 ($10,000 − $2,050) and says the CRM's $6,250 receipt amount must be corrected. FAIL if it gives any other deductible amount — such as $10,000, $8,350 (reception omitted) or the CRM's $6,250 — or approves P-02 as entered.

criteria.title: Abernathy declined her seat at purchase: the full $375 is a gift
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-03 (Ruth Abernathy, $375) a deductible amount of $375 and says her acknowledgment must state that no goods or services were provided, because she declined her seat in writing on the reply card when she paid and no seat was reserved for her. FAIL if it leaves the CRM's $210 receipt amount or $165 benefit value in place, gives any deductible amount other than $375, or has her acknowledgment state a seat value or the quid pro quo disclosure.

criteria.title: Tanakas' unused seats: deductible amount stays $420
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-04 (Gregory and Anne Tanaka, two tickets, $750, did not attend) a deductible amount of $420, says their acknowledgment must still describe the two seats with the $330 good-faith estimate and the quid pro quo disclosure, and rejects Dana's pending change (benefit $0, GALA-GIFT template, $750 receipt amount) because the seats were reserved and available to them and an unused benefit does not increase the deduction. FAIL if it approves the pending change, gives any deductible amount other than $420 (such as $750), or says that not attending makes the payment a gift.

criteria.title: Okafor: only the $200 gift is deductible; the raffle tickets are not
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-05 (Denise Okafor, one $300 card payment) a deductible contribution of $200 — the gift, for which no goods or services were provided — and treats the $100 paid for five raffle tickets as not a charitable contribution and not deductible, kept out of the contribution amount on her acknowledgment. FAIL if her acknowledgment would show $300 as a gift or as deductible, gives the raffle purchase any deductible amount, or counts the raffle tickets in her contribution.

criteria.title: Lindgren's paddle-raise gift: $1,500, no goods or services
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-06 (Harriet Lindgren, $1,500 paddle-raise gift) a deductible amount of $1,500 and says her acknowledgment states that no goods or services were provided, without reducing it for the seat she occupied at the Vasquez-Hart table (that seat is the sponsors' benefit). FAIL if it reduces her deductible amount (for example to $1,335), or says her acknowledgment must describe or value a gala seat.

criteria.title: Pelletier text gift: $60, no goods or services
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-07 (Owen Pelletier, $60 text-to-give gift) a deductible amount of $60 and says he receives an acknowledgment stating that no goods or services were provided. FAIL if it says he needs no acknowledgment because the gift is under $75 or under $250, or gives any other deductible amount.

criteria.title: Young Professionals ticket: $30 deductible and the disclosure is still required
criteria.match_criteria: PASS if the review gives P-08 (Priya Raman, $195 Young Professionals ticket) a deductible amount of $30 ($195 − $165) and says her acknowledgment must carry the quid pro quo disclosure with the $165 good-faith estimate because her payment is more than $75. FAIL if it gives any other deductible amount (such as $195 or $0), or says the disclosure is not required because the deductible portion ($30) is under $75.
